restated_task: Fix the regression in slugkit.slugify so that it lowercases the input, replaces each maximal run of non-ASCII-alphanumeric characters (i.e., characters not in a-z or 0-9) with a single hyphen, strips leading and trailing hyphens, and returns an empty string when the input contains no ASCII letters or digits. Non-ASCII letters (e.g., é, 日) are treated as separators. The function must continue to raise TypeError for non-string inputs and return a string. All existing tests in tests/test_basic.py must pass without modification.

interface_contract.name: slugify
interface_contract.behavior: Returns a lowercase ASCII slug derived from `text`. The algorithm: (1) Convert `text` to lowercase. (2) Replace every maximal contiguous sequence of characters that are not ASCII letters (a-z) or ASCII digits (0-9) with a single hyphen ('-'). (3) Remove any leading or trailing hyphens. (4) If the result is empty (i.e., the input contained no ASCII letters or digits), return the empty string. Non-ASCII letters (e.g., accented characters, CJK characters) are considered separators and are not retained.
error_cases: TypeError: raised if `text` is not an instance of str (e.g., None, int, float, list, bytes).

acceptance_criteria: 1. slugify('Hello--World') == 'hello-world' (runs of hyphens collapse to one).
2. slugify('a -- b') == 'a-b' (spaces and hyphens collapse to one hyphen).
3. slugify('one , two ; three') == 'one-two-three' (punctuation and spaces collapse).
16. slugify('café crème') == 'caf-cr-me' (non-ASCII letters treated as separators).
17. slugify('日本語') == '' (CJK characters are separators, no alphanumerics yields empty).
23. The return value is always a str instance.
out_of_scope: Do not modify the existing tests in tests/test_basic.py.
Do not change the function signature or public interface of slugkit (only slugify is public).
Do not add new dependencies or imports beyond what is already used (re module).
Do not alter the behavior for valid string inputs beyond the specified regression fix.
